requirements.statement: Each legal detector input is an unsigned 12-bit integer in [0, 4095]. This is the synthetic domain, not a claim about a physical ADC.
Detector-attributable SRAM is limited to 2,048 unique bytes under approved accounting scope C-002-SCOPE-001.

For each legal sample accepted at the detector interface, update exactly once. Numerical rolling behavior is determined by accepted-sample order and is independent of elapsed time between invocations. No throughput guarantee is implied.
Compute the exact sum of squares of the newest 32 samples accepted by the detector, in acceptance order. Until 32 samples have been accepted, absent earlier history is zero-padded.
No arithmetic overflow for any legal accepted-input sequence.

Initialization establishes zero history and zero result before the first sample can be accepted. Reset is permitted only while acceptance is quiesced and no accepted-sample operation is in progress. Acceptance remains quiesced through reset completion; after completion, the next accepted sample starts from zero history and zero result.

The result is in [0,536,608,800] and is represented as an unsigned integer capable of that full range (at least 29 value bits). A caller completing an accepted-sample operation can obtain that operation's coherent post-update value; no separate concurrent-reader guarantee is established.
